items.title: An Arhat's Six Constant Abidings, and the Six Elements Composing Any Living Body

items.zh: 又有六種最極清淨轉自所依，第一究竟，無間無缺，無有染污，恒平等住。謂若行、若住，於眼所識色乃至意所識法中，恒平等住。又有六法，是諸色根及所依處，隨其所應之所依止，無有障礙，引導、安養，於彼彼生自在而轉。謂四大種、空界、識界。如是識界，能於現在積集任持福非福業，能引當來愛非愛果。亦能執持識所依止五種色根及所依處，令不爛壞。又由現法後後所生識自在力，令諸有情於善、不善無記業中差別而轉。
items.en: There are also six states of the most utterly pure transformed basis, ultimate in the first degree, without interruption or lapse, without any defilement, constantly abiding in equanimity: namely, whether walking or standing still, with respect to form known through the eye, up through phenomena known through the mind, one constantly abides in equanimity. There are also six things that are the basis for all the material faculties and their supports, on which they respectively depend, unobstructed, guiding, sustaining, and turning freely amid one rebirth after another: the four great elements, the element of space, and the element of consciousness. This element of consciousness, in the present, accumulates and retains meritorious and non-meritorious karma, capable of drawing forth agreeable and disagreeable fruit in the future. It is also capable of sustaining the five material faculties and their supports on which consciousness depends, keeping them from decaying. And through the free power of consciousness arising moment after moment in the present life, sentient beings turn differently amid wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate karma.

items.title: Three Nearly Impossible Barriers and Their Six Antidotes, and the Six Roots of Community Dispute Paired with Their Cures

items.zh: 復有三處，諸修行者難可超越。一者、超越欲貪、恚、害、不樂所攝下界，二者、超越一切行相現行，三者、超越有頂。超越此三難超越處，當知由六種無上對治。四無量是初對治，無相心三摩地是第二對治。我慢永盡是第三對治。永害如是所對治故，諸三摩地皆悉成滿。善修對治故，害所對治，令彼決定不復現行。已斷我慢者，終不為彼我為究竟、為不究竟，如是疑惑纏擾其心。當知有疑惑者，必不離我慢；若離我慢，必無疑惑。又有六種諍根本處。一、展轉相違作不如意；二、覆藏諸惡；三、於等類中，剩受利養執為己有；四、於衣服等更相欺誑；五、違越學處；六、於法於義顛倒執著。又有六法，能斷如是諍根本處。慈心所發身語意業，能斷初二；同受利養，能斷三四；同趣尸羅，能斷第五；同趣正見、能斷第六。
items.en: There are also three places genuinely difficult for practitioners to transcend: first, transcending the desire realm's craving, hostility, cruelty, and displeasure; second, transcending the manifestation of every conceptual mark whatsoever; third, transcending the very peak of existence. Transcending these three difficult places depends on six unsurpassed antidotes: the four immeasurables are the first antidote, the signless concentration is the second, and the utter exhaustion of conceit is the third. There are also six roots of dispute: mutually causing each other displeasure; concealing one's own faults; in a shared community, taking more than one's share of offerings and claiming it as one's own; deceiving one another over clothing and the like; transgressing the communal precepts; and clinging, in reverse, to the teaching's letter or meaning. There are also six things capable of severing these roots of dispute: bodily, verbal, and mental conduct arising from loving-kindness severs the first two; sharing offerings equally severs the third and fourth; shared commitment to precepts severs the fifth; and shared commitment to right view severs the sixth.

items.title: The Six Superknowledges: Five That Draw Beings In, and One That Actually Liberates

items.zh: 又有六法，能攝一切諸修行者威德究竟。謂神境、天耳、宿住、他心、生死智通、能攝威德；漏盡智通，能攝究竟。
items.en: There are also six things capable of comprehending the full majesty and its ultimate completion in all practitioners: the superknowledge of miraculous manifestation, of the divine ear, of past lives, of others' minds, and of death and rebirth together comprehend majesty; the superknowledge of the exhaustion of outflows alone comprehends its ultimate completion.

items.title: Six Obstacles Blocking Direct Realisation of the Truths, and Six Recollections That Lift a Sinking Mind

items.zh: 又於聖諦未得現觀補特伽羅，略有六種能障諦現觀法。謂如前說三種愚癡增上力故、起三顛倒，規求利養，悕望壽命。此中差別者，於順惡見、惡聞、惡說、惡分別處法中，喜樂惡見、惡聞、惡說、惡分別事。如是喜樂，於未得聖諦現觀異生心，最能漂動，極為障礙，非於聖者。是故說此在明分中，非在解脫成熟分中。對治如是能障礙法，當知即是六種正取相。謂如前說五種取相，及一切世間不可樂取相。又有二種具足隨念六行差別，能令心沒諸修行者，正策其心，令生歡喜。謂歸依具足隨念，有三種行：證具足隨念，有三種行。於佛法僧隨念之行，名歸依隨念。於趣涅槃行、趣資財行、趣生天行隨念之行，名證隨念。
items.en: For a person not yet directly realising the noble truths, there are, briefly, six things that obstruct that direct realisation: as already said, through the power of three kinds of delusion, three inversions arise, together with scheming for material support and longing for a long life. What is distinct here is a sixth: delighting in wrong view, wrongly-heard teaching, wrongly-spoken teaching, and wrong discrimination, wherever these occur. To counteract these obstructing things, know that six correct marks are to be taken up: the five marks already described, together with the mark of the unattractiveness of the entire world. There are also two kinds of sixfold recollection that rouse the mind of practitioners prone to sinking, correctly spurring the mind and producing joy: recollection of the [three] refuges, with three practices, and recollection of [one's own] attainments, with three practices. The practice of recollecting the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha is called recollection of the refuges. The practice of recollecting the course towards nirvāṇa, the course towards material resources, and the course towards heavenly rebirth is called recollection of attainments.

items.title: Six Marks Unique to the Buddha's Teaching, a Test for Whether Craving Genuinely Remains, and Why Karma Alone — Never Birth — Determines Destiny: "Six Things" Closes

items.zh: 又有六法，於善說法毘奈耶中立為無上，不與一切諸外道共。謂見大師；聞正法；得淨信；隨學一切所有學處；於大師所起隨念行，謂佛世尊是正等覺者，能說一切法，乃至廣說；又於大師以身語行承事供養。又有六法，能令為盡貪愛修觀行者，決定證知我於今者猶有貪愛，非無貪愛。謂於色境乃至法境繫攝其心。又六因緣故，應知諸業是實可依，非種家姓是實可依。謂下劣種性補特伽羅，亦生不善往於惡趣，亦生善業往於善趣，亦於現法能般涅槃。貴勝種姓，三種亦爾。
items.en: There are also six things, established as unsurpassed within the well-taught doctrine and discipline, shared with no non-Buddhist teaching at all: seeing the Great Teacher; hearing the true teaching; attaining pure confidence; training in every precept without exception; recollecting the Great Teacher — that the Blessed One is a perfectly and fully awakened one, able to expound the entirety of the teaching, and so on at length; and serving and honouring the Great Teacher through bodily and verbal conduct. There are also six things that let one who cultivates contemplation to exhaust craving determine with certainty whether craving genuinely still remains, or does not: namely, whether the mind remains bound and captured by form, and so on through the objects of the other five senses down to mental objects. By six causal conditions, know that karma alone is genuinely reliable — not family or caste. Namely: a person of humble caste may commit unwholesome acts and go to an evil destiny, may commit wholesome acts and go to a favourable destiny, or may, in this very life, reach nirvāṇa. It is likewise so, in all three respects, for a person of exalted caste.

blocks.text: Today completes the sixes. It includes the six roots of community dispute with their cures, the six superknowledges, and a closing statement that karma, not birth, determines a person's worth.

An arhat has six constant abidings: seeing forms, hearing sounds, and so on, with equanimity, neither glad nor sad. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "transformed basis" is the mind itself, "this present thought, continually transformed by precepts, concentration, and wisdom". The **six elements**: earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness compose any living body.

Three barriers are hard to transcend. The third, "transcending the peak", Venerable Miào Jìng reads as conceit: "what is the peak? It is conceit; 'peak' means the highest." The treatise names the exhaustion of conceit as its antidote.

Six roots of dispute in a community, each with its cure. The *Pīxún jì* lists: anger and resentment, concealment and spite, envy and avarice, deceit and guile, wrong view, and inverted view. Communities break along these lines; the treatise's cures are the six harmonies of conduct, speech, thought, precepts, view, and benefits.

The **six superknowledges** (六通): magical powers, the divine ear, knowing others' minds, recollecting past lives, the divine eye, and the **ending of the outflows**. The first five "draw beings in"; only the sixth liberates. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Without the exhaustion of outflows, your first five superknowledges are sometimes lost." Powers are not the goal.

Six obstacles block direct realisation of the truths. Six **recollections** (of the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, precepts, generosity, and the gods) lift a sinking mind (Day 83). Venerable Miào Jìng on recollecting the Buddha as "perfectly and fully awakened": 正覺 is fundamental wisdom, 等覺 is subsequently attained wisdom.

The sixes close with marks unique to the Buddha's teaching, a test for whether craving genuinely remains, and the statement that karma alone, never birth, determines destiny. This echoes Day 51's refutation of caste: a person is noble by conduct, not by family.

quiz.q: In the six purest states of "transformed basis," what does Venerable Miào Jìng say the basis is?
options: the mind — this present thought, continually transformed by precepts, concentration, and wisdom until utterly pure
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "In 'transforming one's own basis,' the basis is the mind — one's own present thought." The reading note takes it as the store-consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: an arhat's feelings are not only neutral; he has uncontaminated joy, pleasure, and equanimity.

quiz.q: The third hard barrier is "transcending the peak of existence." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say the "peak" is here?
options: conceit itself — the "peak" is the highest; the treatise names the exhaustion of conceit as the third antidote
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'Transcending the peak' — what is the peak? It is conceit; 'peak' means the highest." The treatise makes the exhaustion of conceit the third antidote. Even the highest absorption, lacking emptiness, still keeps a self.

quiz.q: The Pixunji names six roots of dispute; the reading note renders 覆惱 as "concealed resentment." What do the lectures say?
options: the six are anger-resentment, concealment-spite, envy-avarice, deceit-guile, wrong view, inverted view; 覆惱 is two afflictions — concealing faults, and lashing out when corrected
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "On these six places are established the six root dharmas of dispute: anger and resentment, concealment and spite, envy and avarice, deceit and guile, wrong view, inverted view." Master Cháng Bǎi: concealment hides faults; spite lashes out when admonished — two afflictions.

quiz.q: The first five superknowledges comprehend majesty; the exhaustion of outflows, its completion. Without it, what happens, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the first five are sometimes lost — the majesty is not ultimate; present at times, absent at others
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Without the exhaustion of outflows, your first five superknowledges are sometimes lost; that majesty is not ultimate — present, yet sometimes absent." Master Cháng Bǎi: the five draw ordinary beings into faith through majesty.

quiz.q: Recollecting that the Blessed One is "perfectly and fully awakened," how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 正覺 and 等覺?
options: 正覺 is fundamental wisdom; 等覺 is subsequently attained wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'The Blessed One is perfectly and fully awakened': 正覺 is fundamental wisdom, 等覺 is subsequently attained wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi agrees: wisdom according to principle and wisdom according to extent.
